title: Romanticism in painting (Delacroix, Géricault)
subject: art
description: Between 1810 and 1850, romanticism revolted against the coldness of neoclassicism. Color versus drawing, passion versus reason: **Géricault** and **Delacroix**.

hero.hook: When painting stops imitating ancient statues to paint passion and scandal.

blocks.text: **romanticism** in painting flourishes between **1810** and **1850**. It is opposed to the rigor of : less cold reason, more emotion, movement and torment. [[neoclassicism]]
With **Théodore Géricault** and **Eugène Delacroix**, painting becomes a mirror of passions and political dramas. By placing color above drawing, they opened the way to impressionism.

At the beginning of the 19th century, the [[neoclassicism]] dominated. Its leader, **Jacques-Louis David**, advocates clarity, balance and morality. The design counts more than the color: one is the intellect, the other the pleasure of the senses.

blocks.caption: David's Oath of the Horatii: the neoclassical ideal of rigor.

blocks.text: At the presentation of *Oath of the Horaces*, spectators fainted at the force of the work: even neoclassicism, before becoming academic, knew how to move.

Romantics want drama, mystery, the violence of feelings. They prefer  or  to Greek heroes, and wild nature to tidy landscapes. The touch becomes more visible, the contrasts more marked. [[Shakespeare]] [[Byron]]

sections.title: Géricault and the Raft of the Medusa

blocks.text: **Théodore Géricault** brings romanticism to the public square with *The Raft of the Medusa* (**1819**). The work is based on a real scandal: the sinking of the frigate *Jellyfish* in **1816**. A captain appointed by royal favor abandons approximately **150** sailors on a makeshift raft.

blocks.caption: The Raft of the Medusa: the agony of anonymous people in monumental format.

blocks.text: Géricault had a life-size replica of the raft built by the same carpenter of the Méduse, a survivor of the shipwreck, to check each plank.

He studies corpses to paint the truth of bodies. On a royal-sized canvas, he shows the agony of anonymous people. At the top of the composition, a black sailor waves a rag at a tiny ship: a [[abolitionist]] gesture and a critique of the elite.

After the premature death of Géricault, **Eugène Delacroix** became the leader of the movement. For him, the **color** carries emotion. Its academic rival, , defends the smooth and precise line. [[Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres]]

blocks.caption: Liberty Leading the People celebrates the Three Glorious Years of 1830.

blocks.text: *Freedom leading the people* (**1830**) celebrates , the revolutionary days of July. The allegory of Liberty walks with the student, the worker and the kid of Paris. [[Three Glorious]]
In Algiers in 1832, Delacroix secretly entered a harem thanks to a port captain. These sketches will feed *Women of Algiers in their apartment*.

In **1832**, his trip to Morocco transforms his palette. There he discovered a new light and partly founded the . He also understands that the shadow is not black, but full of colored reflections: a lesson that the impressionists will remember. [[orientalism]]

Romanticism did not die in 1850: it mutated. By freeing the touch and the color, Delacroix influences **Van Gogh** and **Cézanne**. The artist is no longer a simple executioner of orders: he becomes a visionary.

blocks.text: With them, history painting becomes social criticism. Art must shake up, not just flatter.
Romanticism substitutes passion for reason and the vibration of color for the rigor of drawing. Géricault and Delacroix make individual emotion a universal subject.
